description: Length about 1.5x width; gently rounded jaw and slightly wider cheekbones; the reference 'balanced' face.
key_proportion_rule: Length slightly greater than width with no dominant feature
cheekbone_note: Cheekbones widest point but only slightly
recommended_frame_shapes: Most shapes suit; aviator, rectangle, geometric, wayfarer
avoid: Frames that are too oversized and disrupt balance
rationale: Oval is the baseline proportion so almost any frame works as long as width matches face width

description: Width and length similar; soft curves, full cheeks, rounded chin and jaw.
goal: Add definition and length; create angles
avoid: Round, small, or rimless circular frames
rationale: Angular frames contrast the soft curves and visually lengthen a round face

description: Strong jaw, broad forehead, width and length similar; defined angular features.
key_proportion_rule: Width approximately equals length with angular jaw
forehead_vs_jaw: Forehead and jaw both broad and angular
recommended_frame_shapes: Round, oval, cat-eye, rimless to soften
rationale: Curved frames counterbalance the angular jaw and forehead

description: Wide forehead and cheekbones tapering to a narrow, often pointed chin.
key_proportion_rule: Forehead widest tapering to narrow chin
recommended_frame_shapes: Bottom-heavy, round, oval, light-rimmed, rimless lower
bridge_design: Low bridge to draw eye down
goal: Balance wide top with narrow chin; add width below
avoid: Top-heavy, embellished-brow, cat-eye that widens forehead
rationale: Bottom-weighted frames add visual width to the narrow lower face

description: Notably longer than wide; straight cheek line, may have longer nose or high forehead.
forehead_vs_jaw: Forehead jaw and cheeks similar width
recommended_frame_shapes: Tall/deep lenses, oversized, round, decorated temples
bridge_design: Low bridge to shorten nose appearance
goal: Shorten and widen the face; break vertical length
avoid: Short, narrow, small frames that elongate further
rationale: Deep frames with decorative temples add width and reduce apparent length

description: Narrow forehead and jaw with the widest point at the cheekbones; angular and dramatic.
key_proportion_rule: Cheekbones widest; forehead and jaw narrow
recommended_frame_shapes: Cat-eye, oval, rimless, browline, distinctive brow detail
goal: Highlight eyes and soften cheekbones; add forehead width
avoid: Narrow frames that emphasize cheekbone width
rationale: Frames with detailed or wide brow lines balance the narrow forehead

description: Narrow forehead widening to a broad jaw and chin.
key_proportion_rule: Jaw widest tapering up to narrow forehead
recommended_frame_shapes: Top-heavy, cat-eye, browline, decorated upper rim, aviator
bridge_design: High/decorated bridge to add top width
goal: Add width and emphasis to the upper face
avoid: Bottom-heavy frames that widen the jaw
rationale: Top-accented frames balance the wide jaw by drawing the eye upward

description: Head longer front-to-back relative to its width; narrow when viewed from the top.
key_proportion_rule: Head length much greater than breadth
recommended_frame_shapes: Standard to narrow front; longer temples often needed
goal: Ensure temples are long enough; avoid pinching at front
avoid: Short temples that pull at the temples
rationale: Long heads need longer temple arms and a front width matched to a narrower skull

description: Balanced head proportions; the average reference skull shape.
key_proportion_rule: Head length moderately greater than breadth
recommended_frame_shapes: Standard sizing fits most; no special accommodation
goal: Use standard sizing as the baseline
avoid: Assuming non-standard fit when standard works
rationale: Average proportions are the design baseline most standard frames are engineered for

description: Head broader side-to-side and shorter front-to-back; wide when viewed from the top.
key_proportion_rule: Head breadth approaching or matching length
recommended_frame_shapes: Wider front and hinge-to-hinge; flexible/spring hinges
goal: Provide wider front, more wrap, and spring hinges for comfort
avoid: Narrow fronts and short hinge-to-hinge that pinch
rationale: Broad heads need a wider frame front and more wrap so temples sit comfortably

description: Bridge of the nose sits high relative to the eyes; frames rest naturally without slipping.
key_proportion_rule: Bridge apex at or above pupil line
recommended_frame_shapes: Most standard frames; keyhole or saddle bridge fine
rationale: A high bridge holds standard frames in place so default bridge designs work

description: Moderate bridge height; the average reference for bridge fitting.
recommended_frame_shapes: Standard saddle or adjustable nose pad frames
goal: Use standard or lightly adjustable bridge fit
avoid: Assuming extremes of high or low bridge
rationale: Average bridge height is the fitting baseline; adjustable pads cover minor variation

description: Bridge sits low or flat relative to the eyes; standard frames slide down and touch cheeks.
key_proportion_rule: Bridge apex below pupil line; low nasal root
recommended_frame_shapes: Low-bridge-fit frames; raised nose pads, increased frame curvature
bridge_design: Lowered/wider bridge with raised nose pads
goal: Lift the frame off the cheeks and stop slipping
avoid: Standard fixed-saddle bridges that slip and touch cheeks
rationale: Low bridges need taller nose pads and adjusted bridge geometry to sit correctly
cross_reference: NW-01,NW-02,NW-05,NW-07 (African/Asian wide nose 43-48mm; Farkas Asian/Black significantly wider)
